mechanism_narrative: A sustained upward trend in the federal funds rate signals an intensifying monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates applied to equity cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative during a tightening cycle despite rising FEDFUNDS rates, or the relationship weakens in non-tightening periods (p > 0.05 in t-tests).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in the CPIAUCSL index above 260 signals accelerating inflation expectations, prompting investors to anticipate higher interest rates and sell equities, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative after the CPIAUCSL crosses above 260, or the effect diminishes in non-inflationary regimes (p > 0.05 in t-tests).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in labor demand (PAYEMS) and federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above their 3-month moving averages signals heightened economic uncertainty, prompting investors to reduce equity holdings and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both PAYEMS and FEDFUNDS rise above their 3-month moving averages
regime_hint: tight labor market and monetary tightening
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite both proxies rising above thresholds, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent upward trends in total demand (GDPC1) and industrial demand (RSAFS) above their 3-month moving averages indicate robust economic growth, raising inflation expectations and prompting negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: both GDPC1 and RSAFS rise above their 3-month moving averages
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite both proxies rising above thresholds, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime, sustained high demand (GDPC1) coupled with low inflation (CPIAUCSL below 260) suggests robust economic growth without overheating, fostering investor confidence and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-positive during late-cycle periods despite high GDPC1 and low CPIAUCSL, or the relationship weakens in non-late-cycle regimes (p > 0.05 in t-tests).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained rise in the federal funds rate increases discount rates applied to equity cash flows, compressing future returns and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive during tightening periods despite rising FEDFUNDS rates, or the effect is not significant in non-tightening regimes (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above 105 coupled with a decline in labor demand (PAYEMS below its 3-month moving average) signals slowing economic growth, prompting investors to reduce equity holdings and drive negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO rises above 105 and PAYEMS falls below its 3-month moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite the supply-labor interaction, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.5% signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing consumer confidence and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain non-negative after UNRATE crosses above 4.5%, or the effect diminishes in strong labor markets (p > 0.05 in t-tests).
